use_case: TaraHome blog cover for a homeowner guide to selling a house with smart-home devices
prompt: Create a clean, photorealistic editorial smart-home photograph for a TaraHome blog article about selling a house with smart-home devices and handing the home over safely. Landscape 3:2 composition, designed to remain clear when center-cropped to both 16:9 and 16:10. Show a warm, lived-in but uncluttered residential entryway on moving day: natural oak console, soft daylight, a few tasteful cardboard moving boxes near the edge, and two ordinary adults in a natural mid-distance moment exchanging a simple house keyring and a slim unbranded paper home-information folder. Include only subtle, physically plausible smart-home context integrated into the room—a normal wall thermostat and a standard wall light switch, small in frame, with no screens or readable UI. Warm natural materials, cream walls, restrained dark-forest-green accents in a plant pot or textile, calm practical mood, premium real-estate editorial photography, realistic anatomy, realistic lighting, no product hero styling. Keep the key handoff and entryway centered with generous crop-safe space around them. Absolutely no headline, lettering, labels, logos, watermarks, charts, diagrams, decorative routing or network lines, translucent panels, inset frames, floating UI cards, progress bars, arrows, icons, glowing effects, fake app screens, or invented futuristic devices.
